description: Concrete gun emplacements and defence-building ruins remain on dunes above the eastern beach.
details: The wartime road connected the coastal batteries and carried troops, guns and supplies. Side tracks lead to the surviving fort structures and views over the ocean.

Eastern-beach approach: QPWS describes access 11.3km south of Middle Road, then approximately 400m on foot to the battery and 700m to the lookout. These walking distances are one-way. There is no designated parking area or drinking water.
The official page gives conflicting totals for the longer cross-island walk. Check its current route description before attempting that route.
These are protected heritage ruins. Supervise children, leave relics in place and follow local access signs. Individual bunker and gun-platform positions have not been verified.

name: Fort Cowan Cowan — WWII coastal battery
accuracy: Council heritage-site reference point, not an individual bunker or visitor entrance.
description: Remains of the coastal fort that helped defend the approaches to Brisbane during WWII.
details: Two 6-inch coastal guns and two searchlights were installed in 1938. Reinforced-concrete gun platforms had ammunition magazines behind them. The fort formed part of the island’s examination battery and wartime signalling defences.
The council heritage listing identifies 30 Jessie Wadsworth Street. The broader military complex included other sites; this pin does not identify every structure.
Look for surviving gun emplacements and bunker structures rather than intact operational turrets. Follow signs and respect property boundaries; a heritage listing does not grant entry.
